fixes.explanation: That's the name Elisha gives, friend. He says to look for "…Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi." (2 Kings 9:2). Elisha even names Jehu's father and grandfather. When your errand involves a flask of oil, you want the right head.

Yep, Elisha says to "…get him away from his companions, and take him to an inner room." (2 Kings 9:2). The message is for Jehu, and Elisha has him pulled away from his companions first. I'd say an inner room is about as private as a room gets.

The army commanders are sitting there when the young prophet arrives (2 Kings 9:5), so I see why the army came to mind. But Elisha's plan says nothing about a camp. He says to get Jehu away from his companions and take him to an inner room (2 Kings 9:2).
King it is. The words Elisha gives him are: "I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:3). In the Dorinverse, that is a LOT of news for one flask of oil. And it all comes in one short line.

Israel had judges, whom the LORD raised up, so I see why that word comes to mind (Judges 2:16). But that isn't the word here. Elisha tells the young prophet to say, "I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:3). Jehu is getting the whole crown, friend, not a smaller seat.

Aaron and his sons were anointed to serve as priests, so I see why that one tempts people (Exodus 30:30). But Elisha's words are different: "I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:3). Priests were anointed too, but the title in these words is king.
Staying isn't in the plan at all. After the anointing, Elisha says, "Then open the door and run. Do not delay!" (2 Kings 9:3). There's no waiting around for an answer. Pour it, say it, and RUN.

Yes. The young prophet says, "I have a message for you, commander…" and Jehu asks, "For which of us?" (2 Kings 9:5). Army commanders are sitting there, and Jehu asks which of them it's for. The young man answers, "…for you, commander…" and that settles it.

Jehu does ask. When the young prophet says he has a message for the commander, Jehu answers, "For which of us?" (2 Kings 9:5). With several commanders sitting there, I'd ask too. The young prophet says, "…for you, commander…" and Jehu gets up.

That's the one. The LORD says, "…you are to strike down the house of your master Ahab…" (2 Kings 9:7). Ahab was king over Israel (1 Kings 16:29). Jehu has been serving under that house, and now the LORD hands him this job.

No temple plans anywhere in this message, friend. The reason the LORD gives is that He will "…avenge the blood of My servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD shed by the hand of Jezebel." (2 Kings 9:7). Jezebel was Ahab's wife (1 Kings 16:31), and her name is tied to that blood.

That's the word they use. They ask, "Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?" (2 Kings 9:11). Jehu replies, "You know his kind and their babble…" I've been called worse by a stack of takeout menus from the junk drawer I used to live in.
A spy is a fair guess, but the servants never say that word. They ask, "Why did this madman come to you?" (2 Kings 9:11). The word they pick is madman, not spy.

Right. Jehu says the man talked about "…this and that…" and then repeats the words: "This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:12). The servants pushed, and out came the big news. I'd have cracked the moment they said "Tell us now!" myself.

Army commanders are sitting there (2 Kings 9:5), so news of a battle is an understandable guess. But that isn't what Jehu says. He tells them the man spoke of "…this and that…" saying, "This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:12).
Yes, each man takes his garment and puts it under Jehu on the bare steps (2 Kings 9:13). They do it quickly. A garment is what each man puts down for Jehu.
They sure do. They blow the ram's horn and proclaim, "Jehu is king!" (2 Kings 9:13). Earlier he was sitting with the commanders, and now these men are calling him king.
